title: Best Voice Teacher Software (2026): 7 Tools Compared
description: Voice teacher software compared on published prices and singing-studio needs: backing tracks and warm-ups, student recordings, repertoire, Zoom and recitals.
body:
Voice teachers have a few jobs that a plain booking app doesn't cover. You send warm-up recordings and backing tracks home, hear how a song sounds mid-week, keep track of repertoire for auditions and recitals, and often teach some lessons over video. We checked seven tools that sell to independent music teachers against those jobs. We used only each vendor's own public pages, checked on November 23, 2026. If a vendor doesn't publish something, we say "not listed" or "unknown". We haven't used these tools ourselves and we don't publish ratings.

{{table:trio,nova-music,my-music-staff,fons,mysymphony,tutortally,duet}}

What a solo voice teacher pays (published prices)

US dollars per month before payment processing, for one teacher, with each student having one lesson a week (we count 4 lessons a month). mySymphony Solo charges $0.25 per booked lesson and stops at $20 a month. Its file sharing (PDF, audio, video) is listed only on the Ensemble plan, $15/mo for the first teacher.

Which one fits

  • You send warm-ups and backing tracks every week: Nova Music is the only tool here with a voice teacher page. It lists a resource library for sheet music, backing tracks and warm-up recordings. The library is on the free plan (up to 10 students, 100 MB of storage), and Pro ($10/mo) gives you 5 GB and billing. My Music Staff ($16.95/mo) also shares audio, video and sheet music files with each student.
  • You want to hear how a song is going before the next lesson: Trio lists practice video uploads, so a student can send a clip mid-week and get your feedback. Nova Music tracks assignment submissions with due dates. {{aff:trio|See Trio's plans}}
  • You teach a lot of lessons online: MakeMusic Studio and My Music Staff are the two tools here that list Zoom. MakeMusic says students get a join link when you schedule. Its built-in music library names piano and string titles, not vocal ones, so a voice teacher would mainly be paying $19.95/mo for scheduling, autopay and Zoom. {{aff:fons|See MakeMusic Studio}}
  • You prepare singers for auditions, recitals and shows: Trio and My Music Staff both track repertoire per student. Trio also lists recital running order, RSVPs and printed programs, and you can bill a recurring recital fee. mySymphony lists recital tracking on its Ensemble plan ($15/mo for the first teacher).
  • You teach part-time: mySymphony Solo charges only for lessons you book ($0.25 each, never more than $20/mo). TutorTally is $59.99 once and lets you attach an audio clip to each lesson note, but it only runs on iPhone, iPad and Mac, and families pay you directly.
  • You only have a handful of students: Trio Free and Nova Music Free cover up to 10 students. See our free music lesson software guide for what each free plan leaves out.

Also teach piano? Our best piano teacher software page compares the same tools on practice tracking, method books and makeup credits. Hiring a second teacher? My Music Staff and MakeMusic Studio add $4.95/mo per teacher, Trio adds $5/mo per seat, and Nova Music's multi-teacher plan is listed as coming soon. See best music lesson studio software for multi-teacher studios.

What we couldn't confirm

Whether Trio lets you upload your own warm-up audio or backing tracks for students (its home page lists practice video uploads from students and a lending library, but not file sharing); whether Trio, Nova Music, mySymphony or Duet connect to Zoom or another video service; whether MakeMusic Studio's catalog includes any vocal titles; file size or storage limits for My Music Staff and mySymphony; payment processing rates for Trio, Nova Music, mySymphony and My Music Staff; and annual prices for My Music Staff, MakeMusic Studio and mySymphony. Before you switch, export your student list and run a few weeks of real lessons on a free trial, including sending one backing track and teaching one online lesson. Our software buying checklist lists what to ask, and My Music Staff alternatives covers moving off My Music Staff.

faq: What is the best software for a voice teacher?

It depends on what you need most. Nova Music is the only tool we checked with a voice teacher page; it lists a resource library for sheet music, backing tracks and vocal warm-up recordings, free for up to 10 students. Trio lists practice video uploads and recital tools from $0. My Music Staff ($16.95/mo) and MakeMusic Studio ($19.95/mo) list Zoom (vendor pages, checked 2026-11-23).
Which voice teacher software can share backing tracks and warm-ups?

Nova Music lists a resource library for sheet music, backing tracks and warm-up recordings (100 MB on Free, 5 GB on Pro). My Music Staff lets you upload and share audio, video and sheet music files with students. mySymphony lists file sharing (PDF, audio, video) on its Ensemble plan only (vendor pages, checked 2026-11-23).
Which music teacher software works with Zoom for online voice lessons?

MakeMusic Studio says Zoom is built in: your Zoom link fills the lesson location and students get a link to join. My Music Staff lists Zoom among its integrations. We didn't find Zoom listed by Trio, Nova Music, mySymphony, TutorTally or Duet (vendor pages, checked 2026-11-23).
Can students send me recordings of their singing between lessons?

Trio lists practice video uploads: students submit a clip mid-week and get your feedback before the next lesson. Nova Music lists assignments with due dates and tracked student submissions. We didn't find student recording uploads listed by the other tools here (vendor pages, checked 2026-11-23).
What is the cheapest software for a voice teacher?

Trio and Nova Music are free for up to 10 students; Trio Free takes cash and check only. TutorTally is free for 2 students, then $4.99/mo, $29.99/yr or $59.99 once. Beyond 10 students, Trio Pro is $5/mo (or $50/yr) with no student limit (vendor pricing pages, checked 2026-11-23).
